verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 was the last human moon landing mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972.' 'After a brief 54-year intermission...'; R2: 'Apollo 17 was the sixth and final Apollo mission to land people on the Moon.'; R3: 'for the first time since 1972 during Apollo 17, human beings have left Earth orbit'; R4: references to Apollo 17 as last landing with post-mission dates.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm Apollo 17 as the final crewed lunar landing mission.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley on December 11, 1972.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Astronauts landed on the southeastern rim of the Serenitatis Basin, known as Taurus-Littrow.'; R4: 'On Dec. 14, 1972, following three days exploring the Taurus-Littrow site'
verifications.reasoning: Location directly supported as Taurus-Littrow; date inferred from 'three days' before Dec. 14 and general Dec. 1972 context, but not explicitly 'December 11'.

verifications.claim: Astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over three days on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'following three days exploring the Taurus-Littrow site on the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Exactly 'three days' mentioned; 'over three days' is broader but consistent with actual ~3 days duration.

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan was the final human to step off the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'He was also the last person to walk on the Moon as a part of the Apollo program.'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states Cernan as the last person to walk on the Moon.

verifications.claim: The crew of Apollo 17 was Eugene Cernan (Commander), Harrison Schmitt (Lunar Module Pilot), and Ronald Evans (Command Module Pilot).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Eugene Cernan, Commander... Ronald B. Evans, Command Module Pilot... Harrison H. Schmitt, Lunar Module Pilot'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew roles and names match precisely.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 featured the longest total lunar roving vehicle distance.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Apollo 17 astronauts traversed the greatest distance using the Lunar Roving Vehicle'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states greatest distance compared to previous missions.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 returned the largest amount of lunar samples.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'returned the greatest number of rock and soil samples'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states greatest number of samples.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 returned approx. 110 kg of lunar samples.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention specific quantity of 110 kg.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 was the first mission to include a trained scientist (geologist Harrison Schmitt).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the only Apollo mission to carry a trained geologist to walk on the lunar surface: lunar module pilot Harrison Schmitt'
verifications.reasoning: 'Only' implies first (and last) such mission; directly identifies Schmitt as trained geologist.

verifications.claim: Several uncrewed robotic probes have landed on the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references discuss uncrewed lunar landings post-1972.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the next crewed mission to orbit the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'take astronauts around the moon but not land there'; R3: 'bringing four humans towards the Moon for the first time in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe Artemis II as first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17, involving lunar orbit/flyby.
